questions.subject: GERMAN
questions.topic: The sense of an inseparable prefix inside one verb
questions.learningObjective: Summarise ver- in context

stimulus.body: A glossary defines ver- as signalling change or completion. The participle is verstehen and contains no ge-.

questions.stem: Which statement is correct?

options.text: ver- is separable and takes ge-
ver- is inseparable and blocks ge-
ver- is optional in the participle
ver- requires ge- in the participle

questions.explanation: ver- is an inseparable prefix and blocks the ge- element. verstehen therefore forms verstehen, not geverstanden.

questions.topic: The sense of be- that is not the common one
questions.learningObjective: Summarise the two senses of be-
questions.stem: Cartographer's note for a glossary: how do the two senses of be- differ?

options.text: common sense receives, less common covers
common sense covers or provides, less common receives

questions.explanation: The common sense of be- is to cover or provide, as in bekleiden. The less common sense is to receive or obtain, as in bekommen.

questions.subject: GERMAN
questions.topic: Why a prefix group never takes the participle element
questions.learningObjective: Summarise the no-ge rule
questions.stem: Cartographer's note for a grammar sheet: why do inseparable prefixes never take ge-?

options.text: because they block the ge- element
because ge- is only for nouns

questions.explanation: Inseparable prefixes block the ge- element in the participle. verstanden, bekommen, entfernt, zerbrochen, and missverstanden all lack ge-.
